name: Adam and Eve
text: Eating from the tree God forbade. Given one prohibition in the garden, they ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil after the serpent's persuasion. The first transgression, and the pattern for every one after it: a plain command, a rationalization, a broken boundary. The Lord permitted every tree but one. The woman, deceived, took the fruit and gave it to the man, who ate knowingly. Both then hid, and both shifted blame, to the serpent, to each other, to God for the gift of the other. No death that day, but a sentence on all that followed: pain in childbearing, toil against a cursed ground, and expulsion from the garden lest they eat of the tree of life. Death entered as the long consequence.

name: Cain
text: Murder of his brother Abel. The first murder. Angry that his brother's offering was accepted and his own was not, Cain rose up in the field and killed Abel, then denied knowledge of it to God's face. Warned directly that sin crouched at his door and that he must master it, Cain instead led his brother out and struck him down. Asked where Abel was, he answered with a lie and a taunt: am I my brother's keeper? Not death but a heavier exile: the ground would no longer yield to him, and he became a fugitive and a wanderer. God set a mark on him so that no one would kill him, extending the very mercy Cain had denied.

name: Ham and the curse on Canaan
text: Uncovering and publishing his father's nakedness. Noah drank of his vineyard and lay uncovered in his tent. Ham saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside, who walked in backward with a garment and covered him without looking. Dishonor of a father, in the very thing the law later forbids: the nakedness of thy father thou shalt not uncover. Shem and Japheth showed what honor looks like; Ham showed the opposite and made it public. When Noah awoke and knew what his younger son had done to him, he cursed Canaan, Ham's son: a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. Shem and Japheth were blessed in the same breath.

name: Lamech
text: Killing a man and boasting of it; claiming seventy-sevenfold vengeance. Cain's descendant Lamech, first recorded polygamist, told his two wives he had killed a man for wounding him and a young man for bruising him, and claimed that if Cain were avenged sevenfold, Lamech would be seventy-sevenfold. A killing far out of proportion to the injury, then a song to celebrate it. Lamech takes the protection God extended to Cain and twists it into a license for private vengeance without limit. Scripture records no sentence on Lamech. His line is not heard from after the Flood account opens; the whole world of Cain's descendants ends in Genesis 7.

name: The builders of Babel
text: Building a tower to make themselves a name and resist being scattered. With one language and one purpose, the whole earth settled in Shinar and built a city and a tower whose top would reach to heaven, to make themselves a name and not be scattered abroad. The Lord came down to see it. Direct defiance of the command to replenish the earth, in the form of a monument to human self-sufficiency. The stated aim was a name for themselves, not for God. The Lord confounded their language so they could not understand one another and scattered them over the face of all the earth. The building stopped, and the place was named Babel, confusion.

name: The generation of the Flood
text: Corruption and violence filling the earth. A whole world under judgment. The earth was filled with violence and every imagination of the heart was continually evil, so God resolved to blot out what he had made, sparing only Noah's household. Not one offense but a saturation: corruption of all flesh, violence without restraint, wickedness so total that it grieved God that he had made man. The Flood. Every living thing on the dry land perished; eight souls were carried through in the ark. The waters were both execution and cleansing.

name: The sons of God and the giants
text: Leaving their proper estate; taking wives of the daughters of men. Before the Flood the sons of God took wives of whomever they chose among the daughters of men, and giants were in the earth in those days. The New Testament and the Apocrypha both treat this as a transgression that was judged. Jude names it: angels who kept not their first estate but left their own habitation. Second Peter calls them the angels that sinned. Sirach calls the giants themselves the old giants who fell away in the strength of their foolishness, and the Wisdom of Solomon says the proud giants perished. The angels are reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. The giants and the world they filled with violence went under the Flood; Noah alone was carried through.

name: Er and Onan
text: Wickedness before the Lord; refusing to raise up seed to a dead brother. Judah's firstborn Er was wicked in the sight of the Lord and the Lord slew him. His brother Onan, told to raise up seed to Er by Tamar, deliberately spilled his seed rather than give his brother an heir, and the Lord slew him also. Er's sin is unnamed; the verdict is not. Onan's is precise: he knew the seed would not be his, and each time he went in to Tamar he prevented conception. He took the wife but refused the duty, cheating the dead and the widow. Both died at the Lord's hand, not by any court. The duty Onan refused was later written into the law of the kinsman: the firstborn she bears shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead.

name: Esau
text: Despising his birthright; marrying Hittite wives; purposing to kill his brother. The firstborn of Isaac sold his birthright for a single meal, took wives of the Canaanites to his parents' grief, and when the blessing went to Jacob resolved to kill him. The prophets and apostles treat him as the pattern of the profane man. Hebrews names it: a fornicator or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. His marriages were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah. His hatred of Jacob was murder in the heart. He found no place of repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. Malachi: I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste. Obadiah sentences his house for its violence against Jacob: the house of Esau shall be for stubble.

name: Job's three friends
text: Speaking of God the thing that is not right; condemning the righteous. Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar came to comfort Job and spent thirty chapters insisting his suffering proved hidden sin. Eliphaz went so far as to invent the sins: thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing. When the Lord answered out of the whirlwind, he answered them too. Job had asked them earlier: will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him? They had judged a man on suspicion, condemned the just, and defended God with false accusations against his servant. Job's cause was right; their theology was not. My wrath is kindled against thee and against thy two friends, for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath. They were ordered to bring seven bullocks and seven rams to Job and have him pray for them, lest I deal with you after your folly. He did, and the Lord accepted Job.

name: Joseph's brothers
text: Conspiracy to murder; selling a brother; deceiving their father with a bloodied coat. Ten brothers plotted to kill Joseph out of envy, then sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver and dipped his coat in goat's blood so Jacob would think him dead. Twenty years later they stood before him in Egypt. Envy became conspiracy; conspiracy became man-stealing, which the law makes capital; and the cover-up was a lie that broke their father's heart for two decades. In Egypt they confessed among themselves: we are verily guilty concerning our brother. The famine and Joseph's testing brought the guilt to the surface. Joseph forgave them: ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good. They were spared, and the reconciliation is the founding story of the twelve tribes.

name: Lot's wife
text: Looking back toward Sodom against the angel's command. The angels told Lot's household to escape for their lives and not look behind them. His wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Christ made her a proverb in three words. A plain instruction, given for her own life, disregarded. The look back is treated in scripture as a turning of the heart toward what God was destroying. She became a pillar of salt on the plain, and the Wisdom of Solomon says the standing pillar remained as a monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife.

name: Reuben
text: Lying with Bilhah, his father's concubine. Jacob's firstborn went up to his father's bed and lay with Bilhah, and Israel heard of it. Nothing more is said until the deathbed, where it cost Reuben the birthright. The nakedness of thy father's wife shalt thou not uncover, later a capital offense in the law. Chronicles states the consequence plainly: because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph. Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel. The double portion went to Joseph, the rule to Judah. Reuben's tribe never produced a judge, prophet, or king.

name: Shechem son of Hamor
text: Defiling Dinah, daughter of Jacob. Shechem, prince of the country, saw Dinah, took her, and lay with her and defiled her. He then asked for her in marriage and agreed to circumcision to get her. Her brothers answered with the sword. He had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter, which thing ought not to be done. The law would later require the seducer of an unbetrothed virgin to endow her and the rapist to die. On the third day, while the men of the city were sore, Simeon and Levi killed every male, Hamor and Shechem among them, and took Dinah out of his house. Jacob condemned the manner of it; the brothers answered, should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?

name: Simeon and Levi at Shechem
text: Deceitful covenant; slaughter of a city for one man's crime. To avenge Dinah, the brothers proposed circumcision to the men of Shechem as a condition of peace, then killed the whole city while it was disabled and plundered it. Jacob never forgot it. They answered Shechem and Hamor deceitfully. A covenant made in bad faith, used as a weapon; collective slaughter for an individual's offense; and spoil taken from the dead. Vengeance that belonged to God taken into their own hands. On his deathbed Jacob passed sentence: instruments of cruelty are in their habitations; cursed be their anger, for it was fierce. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel. Simeon was absorbed into Judah; Levi had no tribal land.

name: Sodom and Gomorrah
text: Grievous sin; inhospitality and violence against strangers. Cities whose sin was grave enough that its cry reached heaven. When two visitors lodged with Lot, the men of the city surrounded the house demanding them. Judgment fell the next morning. The prophets later name the fuller charge: pride, fullness of bread, careless ease, and no help for the poor and needy, a hardness that showed itself in the mob at Lot's door. Fire and brimstone from the Lord out of heaven, overthrowing the cities and the plain. Lot's wife, looking back, became a pillar of salt. Held up ever after as the type of sudden ruin.

name: Amalek
text: Attacking Israel's stragglers on the way out of Egypt. Amalek came out against Israel at Rephidim and, as Deuteronomy records, smote the hindmost, the feeble and faint and weary, and feared not God. Israel prevailed while Moses' hands were held up. An unprovoked attack on a nation just out of bondage, aimed at those least able to defend themselves. No fear of God, no cause of war. The Lord swore war with Amalek from generation to generation and commanded that his remembrance be blotted out from under heaven. Saul was sent to execute it and failed; the sentence passed to David and was finished under Hezekiah.

name: Moses and the uncircumcised son
text: Neglecting the sign of the covenant in his own house. On the road to Egypt to deliver Israel, the Lord met Moses at the inn and sought to kill him. Zipporah took a sharp stone, circumcised her son, and cast the foreskin at his feet. So he let him go. The covenant with Abraham required every male circumcised on the eighth day; the uncircumcised man-child was to be cut off from his people. The deliverer of Israel had not kept it in his own household, and it had to be set right before he could speak for God to Pharaoh. The death sentence was stayed the moment the neglect was remedied. The narrative gives no further comment; the priority is the comment.

name: Pharaoh of the Exodus
text: Oppressing Israel; drowning their sons; refusing the Lord's command. The king who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel, ordered their male infants thrown into the river, and when Moses came in the Lord's name answered, Who is the Lord? He hardened his heart through ten plagues and drowned in the sea he pursued Israel into. Forced labor with rigor, infanticide by decree, contempt for the Name, and repeated broken promises: each time the plague lifted he hardened his heart and would not let the people go. Paul says he was raised up for this, that God's name might be declared in all the earth. Ten plagues on Egypt ending in the death of every firstborn, Pharaoh's included. Then his army in the Red Sea: the waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen; there remained not so much as one of them. Wisdom says a strange death.

name: Aaron and Israel at the golden calf
text: Idolatry within weeks of the covenant. While Moses was on the mountain receiving the law that forbade it, the people made a golden calf and worshipped it. The covenant was broken almost before the ink was dry. Impatient at Moses' delay, they pressed Aaron, who gathered their gold and cast a calf; they declared it the god that brought them out of Egypt and rose up to play. Aaron built it an altar and proclaimed a feast. Moses ground the calf to powder and made them drink it. The Levites, called to the Lord's side, put about three thousand to the sword, and the Lord sent a plague on the people. Aaron was spared but not excused.

name: Aaron and Miriam
text: Speaking against Moses; challenging his authority. Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, using his marriage as a pretext to ask whether the Lord had not also spoken through them. God summoned all three and answered plainly. Envy of Moses' unique standing, aired as a grievance. God declared that with Moses he spoke mouth to mouth, not in visions, and asked why they were not afraid to speak against him. Miriam became leprous, white as snow; struck, it seems, as the instigator. Moses interceded, and after seven days shut out of the camp she was healed. A measured discipline, not death.

name: Balaam
text: Divination for hire; counseling Moab to seduce Israel into idolatry. Hired by Balak to curse Israel, Balaam could only bless. So he taught Balak a surer way: draw Israel into fornication and the feasts of Baal-peor and let their own God judge them. It worked, and it killed him. A prophet who loved the wages of unrighteousness, pressed God for permission he had already been refused, and when he could not curse the people, arranged their sin. Christ names the doctrine of Balaam as still at work in the churches. Balaam the son of Beor they slew with the sword when Israel went against Midian, together with the kings of Midian. Jude: they ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished.

name: Israel and the fiery serpents
text: Speaking against God and against Moses; loathing the bread from heaven. Discouraged on the way around Edom, the people spoke against God and Moses: there is no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The Lord sent fiery serpents, and much people of Israel died. Contempt for the provision and the deliverer in a single complaint. Paul cites it: neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents. The serpents bit and many died. When the people confessed, Moses made a serpent of brass on a pole; whoever looked, lived. The Wisdom of Solomon says they were troubled for a small season to be admonished, saved not by the thing they saw but by God. Christ took it as the figure of his own lifting up.

name: Israel at Baal-peor
text: Fornication with the daughters of Moab; sacrificing to their gods. In Shittim the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods. Israel ate, bowed down, and joined himself unto Baal-peor. The plague took twenty-four thousand. Balaam's counsel executed: sexual sin as the door to idol worship. Hosea says they went to Baal-peor and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according as they loved. Psalm 106 adds that they ate the sacrifices of the dead. The Lord commanded the heads of the offenders hanged up before the sun, and the judges to slay every man his men that were joined to Baal-peor. A plague ran through the camp until Phinehas stayed it. Paul: fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

name: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
text: Rebellion against God-appointed authority. Korah led 250 leaders in a challenge to Moses and Aaron, claiming the whole congregation was holy and needed no mediator. The earth answered the claim. They gathered against Moses, charging him with lifting himself above the assembly. It was not merely a personnel dispute but a rejection of the order God had set, framed in the language of equality. The ground opened and swallowed Korah's company with their households, and fire consumed the 250 who offered incense. When the people murmured the next day, a plague killed 14,700 more until Aaron's incense stayed it.

name: Moses at the waters of Meribah
text: Failing to honor God as holy before the people. Told to speak to the rock so it would give water, Moses instead struck it twice and spoke rashly to the people. The water came, but so did a sentence: he would not enter the promised land. God said speak to the rock; Moses struck it and said, 'must we fetch you water?', taking to himself and Aaron what belonged to God, and disobeying the specific instruction in anger. No death, but the leader who had carried the nation forty years was barred from the land for it. A case that measures how much is required of those entrusted with much.

name: Nadab and Abihu
text: Offering strange fire not commanded. Two priests, sons of Aaron, offered fire before the Lord that he had not commanded. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them on the spot. They took their censers, put fire and incense in them, and offered 'strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.' Presumption in the very act of worship, from those who of all people knew the ordinances. Fire from before the Lord devoured them, and they died. Aaron was forbidden even to mourn. A warning that nearness to holy things raises the standard rather than lowering it.

name: The blasphemer in the camp
text: Blaspheming the Name in a quarrel. In a fight within the camp, a man blasphemed the Name and cursed. He was held until the Lord's mind was made known, and his case set the statute for all Israel. The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man blasphemed the Name in the course of a brawl. The offense was against God directly, spoken and heard by witnesses. The Lord commanded that the whole congregation stone him outside the camp, the witnesses laying their hands on his head. From his case came the law: whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.

name: The complainers at Taberah and the lusters at Kibroth-hattaavah
text: Murmuring against the Lord; lusting after flesh and despising the manna. The people complained and the fire of the Lord burned in the outskirts of the camp. Days later the mixed multitude fell to lusting and Israel wept for the meat of Egypt. Quail came, and with the quail a plague. Contempt for God's provision. They said the manna had dried up their souls and named the fish and cucumbers of Egypt as what they missed, forgetting the brick-kilns. Psalm 78 calls it tempting God in their heart and speaking against him. Fire consumed the complainers at Taberah until Moses prayed. At Kibroth-hattaavah, while the flesh was yet between their teeth, the Lord smote the people with a very great plague; the place is named for the graves of the lusters. Paul: these things were our examples.

name: The generation that died in the wilderness
text: Ten provocations; unbelief at Kadesh-barnea. Those numbered from twenty years old who had seen the signs in Egypt and at the sea, and had tempted the Lord ten times, were sentenced at Kadesh to wander until every one of them had fallen in the wilderness. Only Caleb and Joshua of that generation entered the land. Not one act but a pattern: at the sea, at Marah, over the manna, at Rephidim, at the calf, at Taberah, at Kibroth-hattaavah, and finally refusing the land God had sworn to give. Hebrews names the root: they could not enter in because of unbelief. Then, told the sentence, they presumed to go up anyway and were beaten back. Forty years, a year for each day of the search. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness. Sirach counts them: the six hundred thousand footmen gathered together in the hardness of their hearts, whom he pitied not.

name: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath
text: Working on the Sabbath. A man was found gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. Because the penalty had not yet been specified, he was held while the Lord's judgment was sought. The command to keep the Sabbath was already given; his act of gathering fuel was plain work on the day of rest, done openly and witnessed. The Lord commanded that he be put to death; the congregation stoned him outside the camp. A hard case, preserved precisely because the sentence was not obvious and had to be asked.

name: The manna hoarders
text: Keeping manna overnight; going out to gather on the Sabbath. Told to gather only a day's portion, some kept manna until morning and it bred worms and stank. Told there would be none on the seventh day, some went out to gather anyway and found nothing. Distrust dressed as prudence. The first was hoarding against a promise of daily provision; the second was Sabbath-breaking against a double portion already given. Moses was angry at the one, and the Lord at the other: how long refuse ye to keep my commandments? The hoarded bread rotted. The Sabbath gatherers went out and found nothing, and were rebuked. Small, exact, and recorded so the next test would be understood.

name: The ten spies
text: Bringing an evil report; making the congregation to murmur. Twelve men searched Canaan forty days. Ten came back and told the people the land eats its inhabitants and the giants made them as grasshoppers. Caleb and Joshua said the Lord would bring them in. The people believed the ten. They did not deny the land was good; they denied that God could give it. Their report turned a nation from faith to fear in one night and had the people ready to choose a captain back to Egypt and stone the two who believed. The men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord. Caleb and Joshua lived, and forty-five years later Caleb took his mountain.

name: Zimri and Cozbi
text: Bringing a Midianite woman into the camp in the sight of the congregation. While the congregation wept at the tabernacle door over the plague, Zimri, a prince of Simeon, walked a Midianite princess past them into his tent. Phinehas followed with a javelin and thrust them both through. Open defiance of the judgment in progress: not hidden sin but sin paraded before Moses and the mourning assembly, by a leader, with the daughter of a chief of Midian. The offense was against the whole camp's standing before God. Both died on the javelin, and the plague was stayed. God gave Phinehas a covenant of everlasting priesthood because he was zealous for his God and made an atonement. Sirach ranks him third in glory; the Maccabees claim him as father.

name: Achan
text: Taking devoted spoil from Jericho. Jericho's spoil was placed under the ban, devoted wholly to God. Achan took a garment, silver, and a wedge of gold and hid them in his tent. Israel's next battle failed because of it. He 'saw, coveted, and took,' then buried the goods under his tent. One man's hidden theft brought defeat at Ai and the death of thirty-six soldiers before the cause was found by lot. Achan and his household, with the stolen goods, were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. The accursed thing, once purged, restored Israel's standing.

name: Adoni-bezek
text: Mutilating seventy kings. Judah defeated the Canaanite king Adoni-bezek and cut off his thumbs and great toes. He said it himself: seventy kings with thumbs and toes cut off had gathered their meat under my table; as I have done, so God hath requited me. Systematic cruelty to defeated enemies, which he counted as his glory. The law of Israel limits punishment to measure, eye for eye and no more; he had exceeded all measure on seventy men. The same mutilation, once. He was brought to Jerusalem and died there. A pagan king pronouncing the lex talionis on himself is the point of the record.

name: The Gibeonites, and Israel's oath
text: Obtaining a covenant by fraud; Israel making it without asking counsel of the Lord. The Gibeonites came to Joshua in old clothes with moldy bread claiming to be from a far country, and Israel made peace with them. Three days later the fraud was found out. The oath stood anyway. On the Gibeonite side, a treaty by deception. On Israel's side, the text is explicit: the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord. The covenant forbidden with the inhabitants of the land was made through negligence. Because the princes had sworn by the Lord, the Gibeonites could not be killed, but were made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and the altar. Centuries later, when Saul broke that oath, God sent famine on Israel for it.

name: Abimelech son of Gideon
text: Murder of seventy brothers on one stone; usurping a crown. Gideon's son by a Shechemite concubine hired vain and light persons with silver from the house of Baal-berith, killed his seventy brothers on one stone, and had himself made king at Shechem. Only Jotham escaped, and his parable from Mount Gerizim pronounced the sentence. Fratricide financed by an idol's treasury, in pursuit of a kingship God had not given and Gideon had refused. Jotham: if ye have dealt truly, rejoice in Abimelech; if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem, and fire from Shechem devour Abimelech. God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; he destroyed the city and sowed it with salt, and at Thebez a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He had his armor-bearer finish him so it would not be said a woman slew him. Thus God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech.

name: Eli and his sons
text: Corrupt priesthood; a father who would not restrain it. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas treated the Lord's offering with contempt and lay with the women at the tabernacle door. Eli rebuked them weakly but did not remove them. The house fell together. The sons seized the sacrifices by force and defiled worship; the father honored his sons above God by tolerating it. A failure of office compounded by a failure of discipline. Both sons died on the same day in battle; the ark was captured; Eli fell and broke his neck at the news. The priesthood was stripped from his line as foretold.

name: Gideon's ephod
text: Making an ephod from the spoil; Israel whoring after it. Gideon refused the crown and said the Lord should rule, then asked for the golden earrings of the spoil and made an ephod of them and put it in Ophrah. All Israel went a whoring after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his house. The man who had thrown down his father's altar of Baal built a new object of worship out of victory. The text does not say he meant idolatry; it says what it became. The gold of Midian was the same material as the calf. A snare unto Gideon and to his house. As soon as he died, Israel turned to Baal-berith, and his seventy sons were murdered by the son he had by a concubine in Shechem.

name: Israel in the days of the Judges
text: Serving Baalim and Ashtaroth; intermarrying with the Canaanites; every man doing right in his own eyes. After Joshua's generation died a generation arose that knew not the Lord. They forsook him for the gods of the peoples round about, took their daughters as wives, and were sold into the hands of Mesopotamia, Moab, Canaan, Midian, Ammon, and the Philistines in turn. The cycle the book itself describes: the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, forsook the God of their fathers. Judges 3 records the intermarriage that drove it; Psalm 106 says they were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. The anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers. Each time they cried out he raised a judge; each time the judge died they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers. The book ends with no king and every man right in his own eyes.

name: Jephthah's vow
text: A rash vow, and its performance on his daughter. Before battle with Ammon, Jephthah vowed that whatever came out of his doors to meet him on his return would be the Lord's and offered as a burnt offering. His only child came out with timbrels. He did with her according to his vow. The vow itself was the sin: sworn thoughtlessly with the lips, as Leviticus describes, binding himself to a thing God never asked and, on the plain reading, forbade. Ecclesiastes: suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. The text records that she bewailed her virginity and knew no man; readers have long divided over whether the sacrifice was literal or a life devoted, and the text does not settle it. He lost his only child and his line ended with him. The daughters of Israel kept a yearly lament for her. Jephthah is nonetheless counted among the faithful in Hebrews 11, which is the record's own tension.

name: Micah's idols and the tribe of Dan
text: A house of gods, a hired Levite, and a tribe that stole both. Micah of Ephraim stole silver from his mother, returned it, and she had it made into a graven and molten image. He set up a house of gods, consecrated his own son, then hired a wandering Levite as priest. The Danites, migrating north, took the priest and the idols for themselves. Every layer breaks a law: theft from a parent, images made from the stolen silver, a shrine that was not the chosen place, a priest who was not of Aaron, and then armed robbery of the whole apparatus by a tribe that founded its northern city on it. The narrator's refrain: every man did that which was right in his own eyes. The Danites set up the graven image and Jonathan son of Gershom and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land. Dan's idolatry ran unbroken from this to Jeroboam's calf at the same city.

name: Samson
text: Marrying a Philistine; going in to a harlot; betraying his Nazarite vow to Delilah. A Nazarite from the womb who repeatedly went down to the Philistines for women: a wife at Timnath against his parents' counsel, a harlot at Gaza, and Delilah in Sorek, to whom he told all his heart. He woke from her lap shaven, and the Lord had departed from him. Get her for me, for she pleaseth me well: the whole pattern in one sentence. Marriage with the uncircumcised, fornication, and the surrender of the sign of his consecration, each time with eyes that saw what they wanted. Hebrews still lists him among those who through faith waxed valiant. The Philistines put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and set him grinding in the prison house. In the temple of Dagon he prayed once more, and the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life. He died with them.

name: The men of Beth-shemesh
text: Looking into the ark of the Lord. When the Philistines returned the ark on a cart, the men of Beth-shemesh rejoiced, offered the kine, and looked into the ark. The Lord smote them with a great slaughter, and they asked, who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? Even the Kohathites who carried the ark were forbidden to go in and see when the holy things were covered, lest they die. Farmers at harvest opened it for curiosity. The Levites of a priestly city should have known. The text gives the number as fifty thousand and threescore and ten men, a figure long debated; the sentence is not. They sent the ark on to Kirjath-jearim and it stayed there twenty years.

name: The men of Gibeah, and Benjamin
text: Sodomy, gang rape and murder of a stranger's concubine; a tribe that shielded the guilty. The men of Gibeah surrounded the house where a Levite lodged, demanding him; they were given his concubine and abused her all night until she died on the threshold. He cut her into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel. Benjamin refused to surrender the guilty, and Israel went to war. The crime of Sodom repeated in Israel, then compounded by the tribe: they would not hearken to the voice of their brethren to put away evil from Israel. Hosea names it twice as the depth of the nation's corruption: they have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah. After two defeats Israel destroyed Benjamin, the city, the cattle, and all that came to hand; six hundred men survived at the rock Rimmon, and the tribe was rebuilt from them. Israel wept at Bethel that a tribe was lacking.

name: Absalom
text: Murder of Amnon; conspiracy and rebellion against the king his father; lying with his father's concubines. David's son killed his brother, fled, was restored, then stole the hearts of Israel at the gate with flattery, raised a rebellion from Hebron, drove his father from Jerusalem, and lay with David's concubines on the roof before all Israel by Ahithophel's counsel. The stubborn and rebellious son of Deuteronomy 21 on a national scale: murder, treason, and the uncovering of his father's bed as a political act. The rebellion was fueled by a daily lie at the gate: see, thy matters are good, but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee. Caught by his hair in an oak as his mule went from under him, he was run through by Joab and ten armor-bearers, cast into a pit, and covered with a great heap of stones. He had raised a pillar for his own name; the stones were his monument instead.

name: Adonijah
text: Exalting himself to be king; asking for the king's concubine. David's fourth son exalted himself, saying, I will be king, and gathered chariots, horsemen, Joab, and Abiathar for a coronation feast at En-rogel while David lay dying. Solomon was anointed the same day. Pardoned once, Adonijah then asked for Abishag the Shunammite. The narrator notes that his father had never displeased him at any time in saying, why hast thou done so. He usurped a throne the Lord had assigned to Solomon by name. The request for Abishag was, as Solomon read it, a second bid for the kingdom through the king's woman. Solomon had spared him on condition of worthiness. The second offense was the end of it: Benaiah fell upon him and he died. Abiathar was banished and Joab executed in the same purge.

name: Ahithophel
text: Treason against David; counsel of incest; suicide. David's counselor, whose word was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God, joined Absalom, advised him to take his father's concubines publicly, and asked for twelve thousand men to kill David that night. When Hushai's counsel was preferred, he went home, set his house in order, and hanged himself. Betrayal of the king he served, compounded by counsel that made the rebellion irreversible. Psalm 41 and Psalm 55 are read as David's lament over him: mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread. Peter cites the psalm of Judas. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom. He was buried in the sepulchre of his father, a self-executed sentence.

name: Amnon
text: Rape of his sister Tamar. David's firstborn feigned sickness to get his half-sister alone, and when she pleaded that such a thing should not be done in Israel, forced her, then hated her more than he had loved her and had her thrown out. David was very wroth and did nothing. Incest and rape together, both capital under the law he was heir to. Tamar had named the law and offered him the lawful way of asking the king; he would not hearken to her voice. Then he added public shame to the crime. Two years later Absalom had him killed at the sheep-shearing feast when his heart was merry with wine. Nathan's sentence on David's house, the sword shall never depart, began its work here.

name: Baanah and Rechab
text: Murder of Ish-bosheth in his bed. Two captains of Saul's son entered his house at noon under pretense of fetching wheat, killed him as he lay on his bed, cut off his head, and carried it all night to David at Hebron expecting a reward. Murder of a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, as David put it, done with guile for gain. They dressed it as service to the Lord's cause and David's. David commanded his young men to slay them; their hands and feet were cut off and hung over the pool in Hebron. Ish-bosheth's head was buried in Abner's grave.

name: David and Bathsheba
text: Adultery and the arranged death of Uriah. The king took another man's wife, and when she conceived, engineered her husband's death to cover it. The prophet Nathan exposed it with a parable, and David confessed, but the consequences ran through his house for years. David lay with Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite, then recalled Uriah to mask the pregnancy; when that failed, he had him set in the front of battle to die. Adultery, deceit, and murder by another's hand. The child died. Nathan declared that the sword would never depart from David's house, and it did not, his own sons rose against him. David was not executed; he repented, and the throne stood, but under a lasting wound.

name: David's numbering of the people
text: Numbering Israel in pride; a plague on the nation. David commanded Joab to number Israel and Judah. Joab objected; the king's word prevailed. When the count came in, David's heart smote him: I have sinned greatly. Gad offered three judgments, and David chose to fall into the hand of the Lord. The narratives lay the provocation to God's anger against Israel and to Satan; the act is David's, and he owns it. A king measuring his strength in men, as if the Lord had not multiplied them and would not fight for them. Exodus required a ransom for every soul numbered, lest there be a plague among them. Pestilence: seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba in three days. The angel stood at Araunah's threshingfloor with drawn sword when the Lord said, it is enough. David bought the floor and built an altar; it became the temple site.

name: Israel asking for a king
text: Rejecting the Lord's rule to be like the nations. The elders came to Samuel and demanded a king to judge them like all the nations. The Lord told Samuel: they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me. Warned what a king would take from them, they said, nay, but we will have a king over us. Deuteronomy allowed a king on God's terms; Israel wanted one on the nations' terms, to go out before them and fight their battles, as if the Lord had not. Samuel later named it: your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king. Hosea: I gave thee a king in mine anger. The Lord granted the request and sent thunder and rain in wheat harvest as a sign of his displeasure. The people feared and confessed, and Samuel answered, fear not; ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord. They got Saul.

name: Joab
text: Murder of Abner and Amasa in time of peace. David's general killed Abner in the gate of Hebron under cover of a private word, avenging Asahel's death in battle, and years later killed Amasa with a kiss and a hidden sword. David laid both on Solomon's charge. Two captains of the host, both under the king's protection, both killed by treachery outside any battle. David's sentence in life: the Lord shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness. His charge at death: he shed the blood of war in peace. Joab fled to the horns of the altar. Solomon cited the statute that the altar is no refuge for a murderer and sent Benaiah to kill him there, that the innocent blood be taken away from David's house. He was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

name: King Saul
text: Unlawful sacrifice; sparing what was devoted; consulting a medium. A king undone by a pattern of partial obedience. He offered a sacrifice that was not his to offer, spared Agag and the best of the spoil against a direct command, and at the end sought a medium the law condemned. At Gilgal he would not wait for Samuel and offered the burnt offering himself. Sent to devote Amalek utterly, he kept the king and the best livestock and called it sacrifice. Finally, cut off from God, he consulted the witch of Endor. The kingdom was torn from him and given to another. 'To obey is better than sacrifice.' He died by his own hand on Gilboa the next day, his sons with him.

name: King Solomon
text: Multiplying foreign wives; building high places to their gods. The wisest king loved many strange women, seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, from the very nations the Lord had said, ye shall not go in to them. When he was old they turned his heart, and he built high places for Chemosh and Molech in the hill before Jerusalem. Deuteronomy 17 forbade the king to multiply wives, horses, or silver, and named the reason: that his heart turn not away. Solomon did all three. Nehemiah cites him as the proof that even the beloved of God was made to sin by outlandish women. Sirach: thou didst stain thine honour and pollute thy seed. The Lord was angry, and told him the kingdom would be rent from his son and given to his servant, leaving one tribe for David's sake. Adversaries were raised up in his own lifetime; Jeroboam received the ten tribes at his death. So the kingdom was divided.

name: Michal
text: Despising the king in her heart for dancing before the ark. As the ark came into the city of David with shouting and trumpets, Michal, Saul's daughter, watched from a window and despised David in her heart for leaping and dancing. She met him with contempt: how glorious was the king of Israel to day. Contempt for worship, delivered as contempt for a husband. David answered that it was before the Lord, who chose him over her father's house, and that he would be yet more vile than thus. Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death. In Israel that was the end of a line; the house of Saul ended in her.

name: Nabal
text: Churlish refusal of hospitality; railing on the Lord's anointed. David's men had guarded Nabal's shepherds all season. At sheep-shearing David asked for provision; Nabal, churlish and evil in his doings, answered, who is David? and sent them away. Abigail's wisdom stopped David's sword. The Lord did not stop his own. Ingratitude and contempt where the law commands open hands, delivered by a man drunk at his own feast. His wife's verdict: as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. Ten days after his heart died within him and became as a stone, the Lord smote Nabal, that he died. David blessed the Lord who had pleaded his cause and kept him from avenging himself.

name: Saul and Doeg at Nob
text: Slaughter of the priests of the Lord on an informer's report. Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, told the king that Ahimelech had given David bread and Goliath's sword. Saul summoned the priests, condemned them unheard, and when his own guard refused to strike them, Doeg killed eighty-five men in linen ephods and then the whole city of Nob. For Saul, judicial murder of the priesthood on a suspicion; Ahimelech's defense was true and ignored. For Doeg, a report shaped to kill and a hand willing to do what Israelites would not. Psalm 52 is David's indictment of him: thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor. Psalm 52 pronounces it: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place. Saul's own end came at Gilboa. Abiathar alone escaped Nob and carried the ephod to David.

name: Saul's house and the Gibeonites
text: Breaking Israel's sworn covenant by slaying the Gibeonites. Three years of famine in David's reign were traced by inquiry of the Lord to Saul and his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites in his zeal for Israel, against the oath Joshua had sworn. David asked the Gibeonites what atonement they required. Joshua's oath had been sworn by the Lord God of Israel four centuries before. Saul's breach of it was blood-guilt on the land, and the land, as Numbers says, cannot be cleansed of blood but by the blood of him that shed it. Seven of Saul's sons and grandsons were hanged before the Lord at Gibeah, sparing Mephibosheth for David's own oath to Jonathan. Rizpah kept the bodies from the birds until the rain came. Then David buried Saul's bones, and God was intreated for the land.

name: Sheba son of Bichri
text: Insurrection: we have no part in David. On the heels of Absalom's rebellion, Sheba the Benjamite blew a trumpet and cried, every man to his tents, O Israel, and all Israel went up after him. David judged him more dangerous than Absalom. He was besieged in Abel of Beth-maachah. Rebellion against the established government, immediately after the last one had been crushed at the cost of twenty thousand men. A man of Belial, the text calls him. A wise woman of the city asked Joab why he would destroy a mother in Israel for one man; the people cut off Sheba's head and threw it over the wall, and Joab blew the trumpet and went home.

name: Shimei son of Gera
text: Cursing the king and casting stones at him. As David fled Jerusalem, Shimei of Saul's house came out cursing and throwing stones and dust: come out, thou bloody man, thou man of Belial. David forbade Abishai to kill him and later swore he would not put him to death. Solomon inherited the case. Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people. He did it in the king's face, in his hour of weakness, with the king's own guard at hand. His later apology at the Jordan was accepted for David's lifetime only. Solomon confined him to Jerusalem on pain of death. Three years later Shimei went to Gath after runaway servants, and Solomon had Benaiah kill him: the Lord shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head.

name: The Amalekite who claimed to kill Saul
text: Claiming to have slain the Lord's anointed. A young Amalekite came to David at Ziklag with Saul's crown and bracelet and said he had killed the wounded king at his own request. The earlier chapter says Saul fell on his own sword. Either way, his mouth condemned him. He expected reward for the death of Saul. David judged him on his own testimony: how wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord's anointed? Whether he lied for gain or did the deed, the charge stood. Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee. David had him executed on the spot.

name: Uzzah and the ark
text: Touching the ark, transported unlawfully. The ark was moved on a new cart rather than borne by the Levites as the law required. When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah put out his hand to steady it and died at once. The deeper fault was corporate: the ark was to be carried on staves by Kohathites, never touched, never carted. Uzzah's reach was the moment the accumulated carelessness came due. God struck him for his error, and he died there beside the ark. David, first angry then afraid, left the ark three months until he learned to move it the way the law prescribed.

name: Ahab
text: Marrying Jezebel; serving Baal; sparing Ben-hadad whom the Lord appointed to destruction. Ahab did more to provoke the Lord than all the kings before him: he married a Zidonian, built Baal a house in Samaria, and made a grove. He spared the king of Syria for a trade deal after the Lord gave him the victory, and sold himself to work wickedness in Naboth's vineyard. Idolatry, intermarriage, and the release of an enemy God had devoted, on top of the judicial murder his wife arranged for him. Elijah's word: thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord. Because he humbled himself at Elijah's sentence, the evil on his house was deferred to his son's days. His own end was not: an arrow at a venture found the joints of his harness at Ramoth-gilead, and dogs licked his blood at the pool of Samaria as the Lord had said.

name: Ahaz
text: Burning his children in the fire; copying the altar of Damascus; sacrificing to the gods that smote him. Ahaz walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, made molten images for Baalim, burnt his children in the fire after the abominations of the heathen, and hired Assyria against Syria with the temple's silver. Defeated, he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus because they had helped his enemies. Child sacrifice, the sin the Canaanites were destroyed for; a pagan altar pattern installed in the Lord's house; shutting up the temple doors; and the logic of a lost man, worship whoever is winning. Wisdom describes the Canaanites he imitated as merciless murderers of children. The Lord delivered him into the hand of Syria and of Israel, who slew a hundred and twenty thousand in one day, and Assyria distressed him instead of strengthening him. In the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord: this is that king Ahaz. He was buried outside the kings' sepulchres.

name: Ahaziah of Israel
text: Inquiring of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron. Ahab's son fell through a lattice in Samaria and sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover. Elijah met them on the road: is it not because there is not a God in Israel that ye go to inquire of Baal-zebub? Two captains of fifty sent to arrest the prophet were consumed by fire. A king of Israel treating a Philistine idol as his oracle, and then sending soldiers against the man who told him so. The law forbids the ruler to consult mediums and spiritists, and forbids the people to listen to them. Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken, and having no son, his brother reigned.

name: Amaziah
text: Bringing home the gods of Seir and bowing to them. Having beaten Edom with the Lord's help, Amaziah brought back the gods of the children of Seir, set them up as his gods, and burned incense to them. A prophet asked why he sought gods that could not deliver their own people; the king told him to stop before he was smitten. Worship of the defeated enemy's idols, which the law says are to be burned, not carried home. Then, lifted up in pride, he provoked a war with Israel he was warned against and lost. The prophet's parting word: I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this. Israel broke down Jerusalem's wall and plundered the temple; after that Amaziah's own people conspired against him at Lachish and killed him there.

name: Amon
text: Serving his father's idols and refusing his father's repentance. Manasseh's son reigned two years, sacrificed to all the carved images his father had made, and humbled not himself before the Lord as Manasseh had humbled himself, but trespassed more and more. He had both examples in one man, the apostasy and the repentance, and chose the first. He forsook the Lord God of his fathers and walked not in the way of the Lord. His own servants conspired against him and slew him in his house. The people of the land killed the conspirators and made Josiah, eight years old, king in his stead.

name: Athaliah
text: Destroying the seed royal of Judah; usurping the throne. Ahab's daughter, married into Judah's line, saw her son Ahaziah dead at Jehu's hand and murdered all the seed royal to reign herself. One infant, Joash, was hidden in the house of the Lord for six years. In the seventh, Jehoiada the priest brought him out. Mass murder of her own grandchildren for a crown, and six years of Baal worship in Jerusalem: her sons had broken up the house of God and given its dedicated things to Baalim. She heard the trumpets, rent her clothes, and cried, treason. Jehoiada would not have her killed in the house of the Lord; they took her out by the horse gate and slew her there. Then the people tore down Baal's house and killed Mattan his priest.

name: Edom, in the day of his brother
text: Standing on the other side when strangers carried Jacob away; rejoicing over Judah's fall; cutting off those that escaped. When Babylon took Jerusalem, Esau's descendants looked on, entered the gate in the day of calamity, laid hands on the substance, stood in the crossway to cut off the fugitives, and delivered up those that remained. Psalm 137 remembers them shouting, rase it, rase it, even to the foundation. Obadiah: for thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee. Amos: he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually. The law had forbidden Israel to abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother; Edom kept no such law. As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. Malachi: they shall build, but I will throw down.

name: Gehazi
text: Greed and lying to a prophet. Elisha refused payment from the healed Syrian Naaman. His servant Gehazi ran after Naaman, invented a story to collect silver and garments, then lied to Elisha's face about where he had been. Covetousness turned to fraud: he claimed the prophet had sent him, took the goods, hid them, and denied it. He traded the integrity of the prophetic office for money. Elisha, knowing all of it, pronounced that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi and his seed forever. He went out from his presence a leper, white as snow.

name: Hananiah the son of Azur
text: Prophesying a lie in the name of the Lord. In the temple, before the priests and all the people, Hananiah declared that the Lord would break Babylon's yoke within two years and bring back the vessels and the captives. He broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck to prove it. Deuteronomy's test: the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name which I have not commanded him, that prophet shall die. He made the people to trust in a lie and preached rebellion against the Lord, who had told Judah to serve Babylon. Jeremiah: the Lord hath not sent thee. This year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord. So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.

name: Hezekiah and the ambassadors of Babylon
text: Showing all his treasures to Babylon in the pride of his heart. Healed of a mortal sickness and given fifteen years, Hezekiah received envoys from Babylon and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the armor, everything. Isaiah asked what they had seen. Nothing hidden, said the king. Chronicles: Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him, for his heart was lifted up. God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart. A king glorying in his riches before the empire that would carry them away. All that is in thine house shall be carried into Babylon, and of thy sons shall they take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah humbled himself, and the wrath came not in his days: is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?

name: Jehoiakim
text: Building with unrighteousness; shedding innocent blood; burning the scroll of the Lord's words. Necho's puppet king built a great house with unpaid labor, killed the prophet Urijah for prophesying like Jeremiah, and when Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, cut it with a penknife leaf by leaf and burned it in the hearth. Neither he nor his servants were afraid. Jeremiah's indictment: thine eyes and thine heart are not but for thy covetousness, and for to shed innocent blood, and for oppression, and for violence. Withholding wages, murder of a prophet, and the deliberate destruction of the written word. He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem. He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat and in the night to the frost. His son reigned three months and went to Babylon; his brother was the last king.

name: Jehu
text: Executing the house of Ahab, then keeping the calves of Jeroboam. Anointed to cut off the house of Ahab, Jehu killed Joram, Ahaziah, Jezebel, seventy sons of Ahab, and every worshipper of Baal in Samaria, and destroyed Baal out of Israel. But from the golden calves at Bethel and Dan Jehu departed not. Zeal for the Lord that stopped exactly where it became inconvenient to the throne. He took no heed to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart. Hosea adds that the blood of Jezreel would be visited on his house, judging the manner of his executions even where the sentence was God's. Because he had done well in executing what was right, his sons sat on Israel's throne to the fourth generation. Because of the calves, the Lord began in those days to cut Israel short: Hazael smote them in all their coasts. His dynasty ended with Zechariah, murdered after six months.

name: Jeroboam son of Nebat
text: Two golden calves; priests of the lowest of the people; a feast devised of his own heart. Given ten tribes by the Lord, Jeroboam feared the people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he set calves in Bethel and Dan, saying, behold thy gods, O Israel, made priests of any who were not Levites, and moved the feast to a month of his own choosing. Every king of Israel after him is measured by his sin. State idolatry engineered for political security, borrowing the words of Aaron's calf. He was warned at the altar itself by a man of God from Judah, saw his hand wither, and after all this returned not from his evil way. The Lord promised to cut off from Jeroboam every male, and to take away the remnant of his house as a man takes away dung. Baasha killed his son Nadab and all his house. Israel's captivity two centuries later is charged to the sins of Jeroboam, which he made Israel to sin.

name: Jezebel
text: Killing the prophets of the Lord; promoting Baal; witchcrafts. Ahab's Zidonian queen cut off the prophets of the Lord, fed four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal at her table, swore to kill Elijah, and stirred up her husband to every evil. Jehu named her whoredoms and witchcrafts as the reason there could be no peace. A foreign woman ruling a king of Israel into apostasy, with the machinery of state turned against the Lord's prophets. Revelation makes her name the type of the woman who calls herself a prophetess and teaches the servants of God to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols. Elijah pronounced it: the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Jehu had her eunuchs throw her from the window; horses trod her underfoot, and when they went to bury her they found no more than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

name: Jezebel and Naboth's vineyard
text: Judicial murder to seize an inheritance. Ahab coveted Naboth's vineyard; Naboth would not sell his fathers' inheritance. Jezebel arranged false witnesses to accuse him of blaspheming God and the king, had him stoned, and handed the land to Ahab. Covetousness executed through the machinery of law itself: a proclaimed fast, suborned witnesses, a capital charge, and a stoning, every step a mockery of the statutes it borrowed. Elijah met Ahab in the stolen vineyard with a sentence on the whole house. Dogs would lick Ahab's blood and eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Both came to pass.

name: Joash of Judah
text: Forsaking the Lord after Jehoiada's death; stoning Zechariah in the temple court. The boy king saved by the priest Jehoiada did right all the days of Jehoiada. When the priest died, the princes of Judah came and Joash hearkened to them, left the house of the Lord, and served groves and idols. Jehoiada's son Zechariah rebuked him by the Spirit; the king had him stoned in the court of the temple. Apostasy the moment his mentor's restraint was gone, then the murder of that mentor's son for prophesying against it. Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him. Christ counts Zechariah's blood among the prophets' blood required of that generation. Zechariah's dying word, the Lord look upon it and require it, was answered within the year: a small Syrian company defeated a very great host, and his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada and slew him on his bed. He was not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

name: Jonah
text: Fleeing from the presence of the Lord to avoid his commission; anger at God's mercy. Told to go east to Nineveh, Jonah bought passage west to Tarshish. A storm, a lot, and a fish brought him back. He preached, the city repented, and he was angry enough to die because God spared it. A gourd, a worm, and a wind finished the lesson. Refusal of a prophet's commission, with the reason given afterward in his own words: I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful. He would rather drown than see Nineveh forgiven. Then anger without cause, twice, at the mercy he himself had received. Three days and nights in the belly of the fish, out of which he prayed and was vomited on dry land, and the word of the Lord came the second time. The book ends on God's question, unanswered: should not I spare Nineveh? Christ made his three days the sign of the resurrection.

name: Josiah at Megiddo
text: Going to battle against Necho without inquiring of the Lord. The reformer king, promised he would be gathered to his grave in peace, went out against Pharaoh Necho, who was marching to Carchemish and had no quarrel with Judah. Necho sent word that God had commanded him to make haste and that Josiah should not meddle with God, who was with him. Josiah disguised himself and fought anyway. Chronicles is unusually direct: he hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of God. A war without cause, without inquiry, against a warning the narrator credits as divine. The best king since David died of a battle that was not his. Archers hit him in the valley of Megiddo; his servants carried him to Jerusalem and he died. Jeremiah lamented for him, and the lament became an ordinance in Israel. The promise of a peaceful grave was kept in the sense that he did not see the evil that followed.

name: Manasseh
text: Rebuilding the high places; altars to the host of heaven in the temple; passing his sons through the fire; witchcraft; filling Jerusalem with innocent blood. Hezekiah's son undid everything his father had done and more: altars for Baal, a grove, worship of all the host of heaven in both courts of the Lord's house, his children through the fire, observing times, enchantments, familiar spirits, wizards. He shed innocent blood until Jerusalem was filled from one end to another. The record says he seduced Judah to do more evil than the nations the Lord destroyed before them. Every capital offense against God in the handbook's tenth part appears in his reign. Judah's captivity, decades later, is charged to him by name. The Lord brought the captains of the host of Assyria, who took Manasseh among the thorns, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon. There he humbled himself greatly and prayed; the Prayer of Manasseh preserves the tradition of it. God brought him back to his kingdom and he took away the strange gods. But the sentence on Judah for his sins stood: the Lord would not pardon.

name: Nineveh under Jonah
text: Wickedness come up before the Lord. Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. The people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least; the king rose from his throne, sat in ashes, and decreed that man and beast cry mightily unto God and turn from the violence in their hands. The charge is given in one line, their wickedness is come up before me, and Nahum a century later spells out what Assyria's wickedness was: a bloody city, full of lies and robbery, whose prey departeth not. God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way, and repented of the evil that he had said he would do unto them. Jeremiah states the rule: if that nation turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil I thought to do. Christ: the men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation and condemn it.

name: Nineveh under Nahum
text: A bloody city, full of lies and robbery, mistress of witchcrafts. The repentance of Jonah's day did not last. Nahum's burden against Nineveh charges the city with blood, plunder, harlotries, and witchcrafts by which she sold nations; the Lord is slow to anger, and will not at all acquit the wicked. Assyria had been the rod of God's anger against Israel and then gloried in its own hand. Zephaniah names the heart of it: this is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me. The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace dissolved. Nineveh is laid waste; who will bemoan her? There is no healing of thy bruise. Tobit records hearing of its destruction by Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus before he died, and rejoicing over it.

name: Pashur the son of Immer
text: Smiting the prophet and putting him in the stocks; prophesying lies. Pashur, chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesy the city's fall, struck him, and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin overnight. In the morning Jeremiah gave him a new name. A priest using his office to punish the word of God, while himself prophesying comfort that was a lie. The law reserves stripes for the wicked after judgment; he used them on the Lord's messenger before any. The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor-missabib, terror on every side. Thou shalt go into captivity to Babylon, and there thou shalt die and be buried, thou and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.

name: Pelatiah and the princes at the east gate
text: Devising mischief and giving wicked counsel in the city. In vision Ezekiel saw twenty-five men at the east gate of the temple, princes of the people, Jaazaniah and Pelatiah among them, who said, it is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. He was told to prophesy against them. Rulers who reassured the city against the prophets, treating Jerusalem as a safe pot for its own meat, while multiplying slain in its streets. The Lord: ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen. As Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. The prophet fell on his face and cried out, wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?

name: Rehoboam
text: Forsaking the counsel of the old men; forsaking the law of the Lord. Solomon's son rejected the elders' advice to serve the people and took his young companions' line: my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. Ten tribes left him that day. Later, when the kingdom was established, he forsook the law of the Lord and all Israel with him. Pride in the first instance, apostasy in the second. Chronicles: he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord. Sirach calls him the foolishness of the people, one that had no understanding. Shishak of Egypt came up with twelve hundred chariots and took the treasures of the house of the Lord and the shields of gold. When the princes humbled themselves the Lord granted some deliverance, that they might know the difference between serving him and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

name: The captivity of Israel (the northern kingdom)
text: Two centuries of the sins of Jeroboam; secret sins; idols, high places, and children through the fire. Second Kings 17 is the indictment of a nation: they feared other gods, walked in the statutes of the heathen and of the kings of Israel, built high places in every city, served idols the Lord had said they should not, made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil. The Lord testified against Israel and against Judah by all the prophets and all the seers, and they hardened their necks like the necks of their fathers. Hosea's summary: swearing, lying, killing, stealing, adultery; my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight: Assyria carried them away and placed them in Halah and Habor and the cities of the Medes. Deuteronomy had said it: the Lord shall scatter thee among all people. There was none left but the tribe of Judah only.

name: The captivity of Judah
text: Polluting the house of the Lord; mocking the messengers of God; refusing the Sabbath and the land's sabbaths. All the chief of the priests and the people transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen and polluted the house of the Lord. The Lord sent messengers because he had compassion; they mocked them, despised his words, and misused his prophets until there was no remedy. Ezekiel's catalogue of Jerusalem: princes shedding blood, fathers and mothers set light by, strangers oppressed, sabbaths profaned, incest, bribes for blood, usury, priests who put no difference between holy and profane, prophets daubing with untempered mortar. Jeremiah adds the Sabbath gates: bear no burden on the sabbath day, and they would not hear. Nebuchadnezzar slew their young men in the sanctuary, burned the house of God, and carried the remnant to Babylon, to fulfil threescore and ten years until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths. Daniel and Baruch both confess it in the same words: the curse is poured upon us, as it is written in the law of Moses.

name: The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)
text: The image of jealousy; creeping things on the walls; women weeping for Tammuz; twenty-five men worshipping the sun with their backs to the temple. Carried in vision to Jerusalem, Ezekiel was shown four scenes of greater and greater abomination inside the house of the Lord: an idol at the gate, seventy elders with censers in a chamber of painted beasts, women mourning a pagan god, and men between the porch and the altar bowing east to the sun. The elders said, the Lord seeth us not. Idolatry practiced by the leadership in the sanctuary itself, in secret, on the assumption that God had forsaken the earth. The land was also full of blood and the city of perverseness. Ezekiel 14 adds: these men have set up their idols in their heart. The glory departed by stages. Six men with slaughter weapons were told to begin at the sanctuary and slay utterly old and young, sparing only those marked who sighed and cried for the abominations. Mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity.

name: The man of God from Judah
text: Turning back to eat and drink at Bethel against the word of the Lord. Sent to cry against Jeroboam's altar, the prophet was charged to eat no bread, drink no water, and not return the way he came. An old prophet of Bethel lied to him, claiming an angel had said otherwise; he went back and ate. A lion met him on the road. He had refused the king's table and reward; he accepted a colleague's word over God's own. Test the spirits: another prophet's claim did not cancel a command he had received himself. The old prophet's lie is recorded without excuse. The word of the Lord came through the very man who had deceived him: thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. The lion killed him and stood by the body without eating it or the ass; the old prophet buried him in his own grave.

name: The prince of Tyre
text: Saying, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God. Ezekiel's word to the ruler of the merchant city: because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God. Wiser than Daniel, richer by his traffick, and undone by both. Self-deification on the strength of trade. By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned. Tyre had also rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall: aha, she is broken, I shall be replenished. They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? Nebuchadnezzar besieged the mainland city; Alexander finished the island.

name: The prophets of Baal at Carmel
text: Prophesying in the name of other gods. Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal cried from morning to noon and cut themselves with knives until the blood gushed out, and there was neither voice nor any to answer. Elijah's bullock, drenched three times, was consumed by fire from heaven with the water and the stones. Deuteronomy 13 and 18 are the statutes: the prophet who speaks in the name of other gods shall die, and the one who says, let us go after other gods, shall be put to death. They had done it in front of all Israel for years at the queen's table. When the people fell on their faces and said, the Lord, he is the God, Elijah had the prophets taken down to the brook Kishon and slain there. Then the rain came.

name: The shepherds of Israel
text: Feeding themselves and not the flock; scattering the sheep. Ezekiel 34 arraigns the rulers and pastors of Israel as shepherds who ate the fat and clothed themselves with the wool, but did not strengthen the diseased, heal the sick, bind up the broken, bring back the driven away, or seek the lost. The flock was scattered on every hill and became meat to the beasts. With force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. Jeremiah brings the same charge: ye have scattered my flock and driven them away and not visited them. Zechariah's idol shepherd leaves the flock and is cursed in his arm and his eye. Behold, I am against the shepherds; I will require my flock at their hand and cause them to cease from feeding the flock. Then the Lord promises to search his sheep himself and set up one shepherd, his servant David. Christ claimed the office: I am the good shepherd.

name: The young mockers of Bethel
text: Mocking the prophet of the Lord. As Elisha went up to Bethel, the seat of Jeroboam's calf, a company came out of the city mocking him: go up, thou bald head. He cursed them in the name of the Lord, and two she-bears came out of the wood and tore forty-two of them. Contempt for the office, in the city that had made contempt for the Lord its religion. Go up mocks Elijah's ascent, which the sons of the prophets had just witnessed. The Hebrew word covers youths, not infants; forty-two of them were a crowd, not a prank. Leviticus warned that if Israel walked contrary to him, the Lord would send wild beasts among them which should rob them of their children. Forty-two were torn. Elisha went on to Carmel.

name: Uzziah
text: Entering the temple to burn incense, which belonged to the priests. A strong and prosperous king who sought God in the days of Zechariah. When he was strong his heart was lifted up, and he went into the temple with a censer. Eighty priests withstood him; while he raged at them, leprosy rose in his forehead. Usurping an office God had assigned to the sons of Aaron. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death was the statute; Korah had died for the same claim. Azariah said it plainly: it appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah. A leper to the day of his death, cut off from the house of the Lord, dwelling in a several house while his son judged the people. He was buried in a field near the kings' sepulchres, not among them, for they said, he is a leper.

name: Zedekiah
text: Breaking his oath to Nebuchadnezzar; stiffening his neck against the Lord's word by Jeremiah. Sworn by God to serve Babylon, Zedekiah rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar and would not humble himself before Jeremiah speaking from the mouth of the Lord. Warned to the last that surrender would save the city and his life, he feared the Jews who had defected more than he feared the word. Ezekiel names the oath-breaking as the Lord's own quarrel: seeing he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, lo, he had given his hand. Chronicles adds that he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel. Taken fleeing by night near Jericho, he watched his sons slain at Riblah, then had his eyes put out, and was carried in chains to Babylon, where he died in prison. The city and the temple burned behind him. Ezekiel's thou profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day is come.

name: Belshazzar
text: Drinking from the temple vessels and praising the gods of gold and silver. At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar called for the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the house of God in Jerusalem, drank wine from them with his wives and concubines, and praised the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. Fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster. Daniel's indictment: thou hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven, and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified. He knew what had happened to his father and humbled not his heart. Mene, mene, tekel, upharsin: numbered, weighed and found wanting, divided. In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom.

name: Daniel's accusers
text: Conspiring by law against an innocent man. Finding no fault in Daniel except concerning the law of his God, the presidents and princes flattered Darius into signing a decree that no one might petition any god or man for thirty days, then caught Daniel praying. The king labored till sunset to deliver him and could not. A snare built from the machinery of law itself: a statute designed to make righteousness a crime, and a king manipulated into executing it. Deuteronomy's rule for a false witness is that what he thought to do to his brother be done to him. Daniel came out of the den without a mark because he believed in his God. The king commanded those who had accused him, with their children and wives, cast into the den; the lions broke all their bones before they reached the bottom.

name: Eliashib and Tobiah the Ammonite
text: Lodging an Ammonite enemy in a chamber of the house of God; a priest's house allied to Sanballat.
